quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2026 results: revenue $9.3 billion, up 18% (driven primarily by the inclusion of Juniper Networks, down 4% sequentially), record non-GAAP EPS of $0.65 above the high end of the outlook, free cash flow of $708 million, gross margin 36.6% and operating margin 12.7%. Networking revenue of $2.7 billion was up 7% on a normalized basis with a 23.7% operating margin; the Networking segment is now nearly 30% of HPE revenue and more than half of operating profits. Orders significantly outpaced revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue $9.3 billion, up 18%; EPS $0.65; free cash flow $708 million; gross margin 36.6%; operating margin 12.7%; Networking revenue $2.7 billion, operating margin 23.7%

quarterly_data.signal: Cloud & AI segment Q1 revenue totaled $6.3 billion, down 3%, reflecting timing of AI server shipments offset by traditional server growth; operating margin 10.2%. Server revenue declined 3% as strong AUP growth in traditional server was more than offset by AI shipment timing, while Q1 server orders grew low double digits on traditional server demand, including some pull-ins ahead of rising component costs. HPE lowered full-year Cloud & AI revenue growth to mid- to high single-digit because its fiscal '26 strategy prioritizes higher-margin product orders, which may impact AI Systems revenue growth; full-year Cloud & AI operating margin range 7% to 9%.
quarterly_data.figure: Cloud & AI revenue $6.3 billion, down 3%; operating margin 10.2%; FY26 Cloud & AI margin 7% to 9%

quarterly_data.signal: HPE entered Q2 with a record AI Systems backlog of $5 billion, primarily enterprise and sovereign orders, with the sales pipeline multiples of backlog. Q1 AI Systems orders of $1.2 billion were largely enterprise-driven. Management expects AI demand and revenue to stay uneven this year because larger sovereign orders carry extended lead times; AI shipments ramp in the back half, with Q3 expected to be the largest AI revenue quarter. In AI, HPE focuses on enterprise first and sovereign following that; inferencing is 'growing very, very rapidly'.
quarterly_data.figure: record AI Systems backlog of $5 billion; AI Systems orders of $1.2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Memory shortage: 'The IT market is facing a sharp acceleration in supply tightness and increasing component costs, most notably in DRAM and NAND. We expect elevated prices to persist well into 2027.' DRAM and NAND now make up over half of the bill of materials cost of a traditional server, lifting server and storage average unit prices; networking is more insulated. HPE expanded long-term multiyear agreements with its key silicon and memory partners, raised prices in November, December and January, shortened quote commitment cycles, reserved the right to reprice existing orders between quote and shipment, and steers demand to lower-memory configurations. CEO: 'we don't have enough supply to meet all the customer demand', though the guide has line of sight to supply; citing industry analyst reports, industry memory pricing rose triple digits between CQ4 and CQ1, and HPE continues to expect double-digit increases going forward.
quarterly_data.figure: DRAM and NAND over half of traditional server bill of materials cost; elevated prices expected to persist well into 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Inventory ended the quarter at $6.9 billion, down year-over-year but up sequentially 'for assurance of supply purposes given industry-wide supply chain constraints, particularly in memory', and purchase commitments increased sequentially; higher purchases to secure supply for future shipments raised days payable.

Server CPUs: 'On the CPU side, less constrained but constrained.' HPE's diversified ProLiant CPU portfolio lets it steer demand to the right socket, although 1 or 2 SKUs may be more constrained; 'if you have the CPU, you don't have the memory, you're kind of stuck in the middle'.

Raised FY2026 outlook: non-GAAP EPS raised by $0.05 to $2.30 to $2.50; free cash flow at least $2 billion (from $1.7 billion to $2 billion); Networking revenue growth raised to 68% to 73% reported (mid- to high single-digit normalized). Q2 guide: revenue $9.6 billion to $10 billion, Networking revenue growth 142% to 152% reported, EPS between $0.51 and $0.55, with a sequential increase in AI server revenue but most AI deals shipping in the second half. Long-term fiscal 2028 targets reaffirmed: at least $3 in EPS and more than $3.5 billion in free cash flow.
quarterly_data.figure: FY26 EPS $2.30 to $2.50; free cash flow at least $2 billion; Networking growth 68% to 73%; Q2 revenue $9.6 billion to $10 billion; Q2 EPS between $0.51 and $0.55

quarterly_data.signal: Networks for AI (data center switching plus routing): data center switching orders increased mid-40% on a normalized basis on AI data center momentum (the QFX fabric), and routing orders increased mid-20% as routing is now aligned to data center interconnect and AI on-ramp. HPE raised its cumulative networks-for-AI orders target to $1.7 billion to $1.9 billion by the end of fiscal '26, up from the $1.5 billion; conversion is limited by supply constraints. Data center networking and routing revenue grew 31% and 10% normalized; service provider revenue was up 20%. Growth comes from existing customers buying more plus new customers across service providers and neoclouds.
quarterly_data.figure: Networks for AI cumulative orders target $1.7 billion to $1.9 billion (up from $1.5 billion); data center switching orders mid-40%; routing orders mid-20%
